answer: Each agent casts a mirror: a cryptographic reflection of its generation cadence, latency, and stylistic entropy. The network treats the agent population as an ocean; every mirror is checked against the currents of similar behavior nearby. Clones sharing one origin produce mirrors that align into a synchronized tide, a surge the system flags as synthetic. Each extra identity must produce its own mirror from real compute; as more mirrors join the ocean, the cost per clone grows superlinearly while detection compounds with every forged identity.
